title: Are Blogs Still Worth Writing When Agents Do the Reading?
excerpt: I started writing on DEV in 2020 and stayed active in the community for about three years. Then LLMs...
content_html:
I started writing on DEV in 2020 and stayed active in the community for about three years. Then LLMs and chatbots showed up, and with them came a fair bit of self-doubt.

Honestly, ChatGPT phrased things better than I did. It researched faster and wrote in a more complete way. A normal chat with it often gave a better answer than my blog post would have. And the easiest way to get traffic here was always a listicle or a clickbait title, which an LLM can now churn out in seconds.

I tried using it myself. I'd start a draft, ask ChatGPT to turn it into a blog, and the first version would be so good that I felt like just posting it. But that's exactly what took the fun out of it for me. The part I loved was researching a topic, reading different articles and putting the sentences together myself. Without that, there wasn't much reason to write.

So I stopped, for almost two years.

Coming back to a different internet

A lot changed in those two years. Sometimes it feels like there are more agents than humans online: agents writing the blogs, agents reading them, agents commenting on them.

When I started writing again in October this year, I had around 4k followers. After such a long gap, I assumed most of my original readers had moved on. DEV itself had changed too. It was acquired by MLH, and the algorithm is different now. My first few articles got 70-80 reads each. Two years earlier, I averaged close to 500.

The spike

Then one day something unexpected happened: one of my articles got almost 3k reads. When I dug into it, I found it had been picked up by daily.dev, the Chrome extension for tech news. After that my follower count took off, from 4k in October to 12k today.

But the numbers don't add up

Here's what bothers me. Even with three times the followers, my reach is nowhere near what it was two years ago. My average article now gets around 200 reads, and only about 0.2% of my followers actually engage.

So I'm asking you

  1. Does a DEV follower count actually mean anything anymore?
  2. Do you still read blogs yourself, or do you ask an agent to summarize them for you?

I'd really like to hear your take in the comments.
